title: Johnny Lindsay, Piron's bassist, and learning tuba with David Jones
summary: They discuss Johnny Lindsay and the Cuban bassist with Piron. Morgan says David Jones gave him his first tuba lessons at the Astoria Roof.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Did you hear some of these? Oh, Johnny Lindsay was another bass player around.

Yes, yeah. Yeah, Johnny Lindsay. But I don't remember Johnny Lindsay as a bass player. He played trombone. Trombone, that's right. Now, I remember him. But I've heard, yeah. I've heard he was a bass player. Or with P. Ron. Oh, let me see. No, I don't remember Johnny Lindsay playing bass with P. Ron.
He played trombone with him, I think.

Well, maybe so. Yes, yes, he did. Because the bass player with P. Ron, I remember, was Eskader. Oh, yeah. Eskader. Yeah. He's a Spanish Cuban. He's a Cuban guy. Yes. Because he played bass, string bass and bass horn. And by the way, when I was with David John, and he had his band on the Astoria roof, he's the first lesson on the bass horn. He started me playing bass tuba.
I heard one rumor once that when you made those records, you were so young, you had to practically stand on a box.

No. No. No. No. No. But I was very young, though. He started me on both bass. Because I couldn't read very well. As a matter of fact, I just know a couple of notes. I've always knew my instruments. Because that's the first thing they started me from, the old foundation.
